column1: # 032 contract 18 — the historical-replay corpus.
#   commit<TAB>test<TAB>evidence<TAB>note
# `evidence` is `observed` or `asserted`, and the difference is the whole point:
#   observed  the test was RUN at commit^ and at commit and changed its verdict.
#             The only kind that counts towards recall.
#   asserted  somebody read the commit and concluded the test would have caught it.
#             Recorded so the candidate is not lost, and excluded from the figure —
#             a recall computed over beliefs measures the beliefs.
# THIS FILE IS EMPTY OF OBSERVED ENTRIES, and the gate says so rather than printing
# 100% over nothing. 032 §6 calls historical replay "the ground-truth oracle and the
# one that would catch a real design flaw"; over an empty corpus it is not one.
# Establishing an entry: build VPP at commit^ and at commit, run the named test at
# both, confirm it fails then passes. Verified 2026-08-05 that this is possible here
# — `make test TEST=<name>` needs no root and no network namespaces, correcting a
# premise this project carried for weeks.
# CANDIDATES PROBED AND REJECTED. Kept so the expensive probe is not repeated.
# 1d0e0e825  pvti: fix adjacent packet overwrite with very big packets
#            test_pvti — REJECTED 2026-08-05.
#            `test_0003_pvti_send_simple_1pkt_big` exists at the parent and looked
#            like exactly the right shape. It PASSES at the parent: the suite does
#            not exercise the overwrite. Built and ran both revisions to find that
#            out, which is the point of `observed` — reading the commit message
#            would have produced a confident wrong entry.
# A BETTER METHOD, for whoever picks this up
# Hunting for a commit whose fix an existing test happens to catch is a poor use
# of ~40 minutes per attempt, and the pvti result shows why: the plausible
# candidate was wrong.
# Instead REVERT a historical fix's src/ diff on top of HEAD and run the suite.
# Whatever fails is the ground truth, observed rather than guessed, and it uses
# the current build instead of two checkouts. That is the mutation gate's own
# methodology applied to a change somebody else made for their own reasons —
# which is the whole difference 032 §6 draws between the two harnesses.
# The entry then records the original commit; the diff replayed for selection is
# still `commit^..commit`, so nothing about what the gate measures changes.
